Privacy Policy

Last Updated: June 8, 2026

TL;DR: We have zero access to your data.

SafeSpot requires no app-specific account and uses no developer backend for your content. Your data remains available offline and synchronizes through your private iCloud database. We do not collect telemetry, analytics, or crash reports.

1. Data Storage

Data you enter into SafeSpot, including item names, locations, private notes, reminder settings, and photos, is stored locally for offline use and synchronized through Apple's CloudKit service in your private iCloud database.

SafeSpot does not operate a backend server and does not receive your saved content. Deleting the app removes its local copy; data synchronized with iCloud may remain available to SafeSpot on your other devices or after reinstalling.

2. Data Collection and Tracking

SafeSpot does not collect any personal data.

  • No analytics SDKs (e.g., Google Analytics, Mixpanel, Firebase).
  • No crash reporting SDKs (e.g., Crashlytics, Sentry).
  • No advertising or third-party tracking networks.

Apple may collect anonymized crash reports or usage metrics if you have explicitly opted into sharing this data with App Developers in your overall iOS settings, but this is handled entirely by Apple's OS, not our app code.

3. Local Authentication (Face ID / Touch ID)

SafeSpot offers a feature to lock the app using Face ID, Touch ID, or your device passcode. This utilizes Apple's LocalAuthentication framework. The biometric authentication happens entirely on your device's Secure Enclave. The app only receives a "success" or "failure" signal; it never has access to your actual biometric data.

4. Photos and Camera Access

If you choose to attach photos to your items, SafeSpot uses the native iOS PhotosUI picker. We only have access to the specific photos you select. Photos are stored locally and synchronized as encrypted CloudKit assets in your private iCloud database.

5. Notifications

SafeSpot uses local notifications to remind you to check your items. Reminder alerts are scheduled and triggered locally. CloudKit uses silent Apple Push Notification service messages to notify the app about synchronization changes; these are not marketing notifications and do not contain your reminder alert text.

6. Changes to This Privacy Policy

We may update our Privacy Policy from time to time. Since we cannot email you (we don't have your email address), any updates will be reflected on this page and noted in the App Store release notes.

7. Contact Us

If you have any questions or suggestions about our Privacy Policy, do not hesitate to contact us at the details provided on our Support page.
